scope: Dated public Cloud Storage contract baseline and emulator project requirements.
counting_rules: Rows are implementation tracking units, not independent product capabilities or estimated effort.
Keep api_operation, behavior and project_requirement denominators separate.
REST, XML, native RPC, shared interfaces and MCP are deliberately separate transport surfaces.
Schema fields and query parameters are tracked in separate inventories, not added to feature totals.
A phase identifies the first recommended implementation focus, not permission to mark the entire row complete.
Decompose selected rows into acceptance cases; record only executed tests and existing evidence.

delivery_plan.semantics: Planning metadata only. Feature statuses, fidelities, acceptance results and verification records below remain authoritative and unchanged. Existing scope references describe executed subsets, not new IMPLEMENTED claims.
delivery_plan.phase_rule: P0-P7 remain coverage groups, not execution gates. Preserve the delivered basic JSON/CORS/HTTPS prerequisites for signing. Prioritize distribution and familiar configuration, then independent initializer, directory-sync and source-import tracks, then broader reference and Rails work. Order is a selection preference, not an implicit dependency: use depends_on for readiness. Existing SDK/browser checks and ready independent tracks may run early. Shared state changes have one integration owner; adapters do not bypass catalog/publication logic. Complete the pinned-reference superset and named extensions before 1.0.0; publish useful increments as 0.x releases.
delivery_plan.progress_rule: Report completed, evidence-backed deliverables against a frozen selected delivery scope, separately from API/behavior/project counts. Do not assign PARTIAL a fractional weight, double-count overlapping feature references, or infer gate completion from this plan.
common_completion_gate: Use pinned reference capabilities and representative existing-client workflows as the minimum functional baseline for each affected feature. Preserve source-supported inputs, response information and state effects; narrower native scopes and additional strict checks are not proof of feature parity. Add capabilities above that baseline without breaking the selected compatibility profile.
Freeze the supported protocol, profile, fields, limits and explicit exclusions before implementation; reconcile the affected official sources and gaps.
Name positive, negative, boundary, authorization and interaction acceptance cases; pass wire and relevant pinned SDK/CLI/container checks.
Verify applicable atomicity, interruption, restart/recovery, resource bounds and clock behavior; measurements are required for performance claims.
Resolve every deviation within the declared scope; keep simulations and external-service boundaries explicit. Later scope extensions do not reopen a passed scope unless it regresses.

Record commands, outcomes, test IDs, evidence and verification date in the existing feature records; regenerate compatibility views. The unchanged IMPLEMENTED policy still applies to whole feature rows.
Gate closure requires evidence for every completion condition, not only the linked historical cases. These planning entries have no independent implementation status.

Review the pinned fake-gcs-server migration contract before each slice; add relevant legacy-profile cases without weakening the independent strict/Google-contract corpus. Document native GCS_MIMIC_ equivalents by role; identical flag spelling and environment suffixes are not required.

environment_contract.precedence: CLI overrides environment; contradictory renamed/native settings at the same precedence fail deterministically.
environment_contract.storage_boundary: DATA is seed input; DATA_DIR is destination persistence. FILESYSTEM_ROOT requires explicit source conversion, not in-place reinterpretation.
environment_contract.port_boundary: Existing Compose GCS_MIMIC_PORT means host publication, not the process listener; keep container/server mappings separate.

migration.storage_contract: Prefer a transactional metadata catalog plus bounded opaque immutable files; keep foreign seed/filesystem/live-export readers separate from internal persistence. Preserve original data and identities, block lossy import, and validate coherent backup/recovery before cutover. SQLite is the current justified default, not a universal performance winner.

configuration_contract.requirement: Support familiar server configuration roles and independent per-bucket extensions without requiring identical fake-gcs-server option names. Keep listener, advertised API URL, public URL construction and host routing distinct.
configuration_contract.current_boundary: Native server options, per-bucket JSON APIs and a version-1 create-missing initialization file exist. A combined public-host option remains separate. This entry describes requirements; feature rows own implementation status.
configuration_contract.initialization_policy: Use a file to create missing buckets with individual settings, then allow API changes. Preserve existing settings and objects on every restart; file changes do not overwrite existing buckets, and removing an entry does not delete a bucket.
acceptance_targets: Validate the complete initialization input and reject duplicate bucket names before any mutation; reuse shared bucket field, authorization and unsupported-setting checks.
Verify two buckets with different CORS and versioning settings, API updates, restart preservation and independent object effects.
Verify deterministic recovery/retry after partial initialization and document how missing buckets are completed without resetting existing state.
Document source-to-native startup examples for scheme, listen, data, external-url and public-host roles without claiming aliases or equivalent host filtering.

filesystem_sync_contract.requirement: Provide a configured, inspectable bucket/object directory with bidirectional synchronization: external additions, edits and deletions reach the API, and API mutations appear in the same directory. A one-time seed import or migration converter does not satisfy this requirement.
filesystem_sync_contract.current_boundary: The current implementation has one-time read-only seeding and opaque immutable internal blobs, without directory watching or write-back. docs/en/slices/directory-synchronization.md freezes the local contract and settings; every new runtime case remains PENDING and DESIGN-062, DESIGN-072 and DESIGN-074 remain PARTIAL. DESIGN-076 is unchanged.
filesystem_sync_contract.catalog_boundary: SQLite may remain the metadata/index catalog. External changes must use shared bounded ingestion, checksum, generation and atomic-publication logic; do not mutate committed internal blobs in place or update only catalog size/path fields.
acceptance_targets: Verify API/external create, overwrite, delete and rename in both directions, including multiple buckets and persistence of independent bucket settings.
Handle editor temporary files, partial writes, atomic replacement, self-generated events and duplicate or missed notifications without stale hashes or update loops.
Define API/external conflict behavior and visible synchronization failures before implementation; verify no silent data loss and preserve retained generations.
Define portable name mapping, file/directory collisions and symlink policy; reject unrepresentable state explicitly.
Verify bounded rescan and restart/recovery across the visible directory, immutable blobs and SQLite before claiming compatibility.
open_decisions: sync-watcher must obtain owner approval before selecting a file-notification dependency and verify Windows/native/bind-mount notification support; no library is selected by sync-contract.
Shared state chooses its internal identity/state/journal/admission/recovery mechanisms and benchmark thresholds; the directory synchronization contract requests properties and acceptance cases only.

full_superset_gate: Inventory all public source flags/settings, routes, helper/event behavior, backend modes, Go APIs and Storage v1 gRPC; do not silently drop surfaces missing from the current GCS inventory.
Pass the pinned source corpus, representative unchanged clients and migration-preservation cases; legacy emulation and strict Google-contract behavior have separate expectations.
Retain names, bytes, headers/metadata, source identities, ACL/bucket settings and archived versions where exposed; unsupported or inconsistent source state blocks a lossless migration claim.
Verify source immutability, bounded dry-run/import, interruption/retry, resource budgets, endpoint cutover and rollback without losing post-cutover writes.
Report baseline version, profile, supported platforms and remaining gaps; partial releases cannot advertise full replacement. New versions explicitly extend the baseline.

Reserve product 1.0.0 for this complete gate plus the fixed additions: independent bucket settings, create-missing file initialization with preserved API updates, bidirectional directory sync, strict local authorization/V4 RSA validation and persistent version history. Full Google API coverage is a separate goal; follow docs/en/release-policy.md.

milestones.title: Convert durable source data without loss
completion_conditions: Implement source-filesystem-reader and source-integrity-report from docs/en/slices/source-storage-contract.md using explicit root-wide metadata mode and the pinned bucket/object git blobs; never mutate source, silently fall back between xattrs/sidecars or infer memory state from a directory.

Preflight metadata/stat only into a separate empty destination; preserve recoverable normalized disk names, bytes, fields, generations and exact Created/Updated microseconds. Report generated ETags/bucket times/metageneration and unverifiable original names; block ACL/history/retention, ambiguity, corruption and nonzero sub-microsecond digits without a lossy ms mode. shared-timestamp-precision provides schema 14 storage; imported publication remains in shared-imported-identity.

Use staging-only verified publication, shared-imported-identity and shared-import-journal with imported hold preservation; see Delivery boundaries in docs/en/slices/source-storage-contract.md and owning feature known_deviations for unresolved Shared state handoffs. publish_objects uses per-element SAVEPOINTs and atomically records successful elements with digests, inode/ctime observations and journal state. Close count/time-bounded batches without rollback; element rejection is terminal and resumable progress is a contiguous prefix. A possibly committed blob survives caller cancellation during SQLite commit and handle drop; definitely uncommitted, unreferenced excluded/unattempted/cancelled staging blobs are reclaimed before command exit. Cleanup failures stay visible off Tokio workers; handle budgeting remains unresolved. Verify bodies once while staging; retain inode/ctime in within-execution fingerprints and stop on stat-only change, then revalidate drifted committed elements on resume. This limited no-reread exception was coordinator-approved on 2026-10-24. Retry interruption/cancellation/Busy/disk-full or inode/ctime-only stops only for an unchanged export binding, including crashes before/after recording the stat-only stop. Changes to paths/size/mtime/metadata/body, corruption, checksum/blocking findings and element rejection remain terminal with safe abandonment guidance.

Pass source-name-scope, source-preserved-identity, source-import-authorization, source-import-recovery and source-cutover: AdminGrant in both profiles, no imported IAM/public grants, strict reads, old generation conditions, nonreused identities, shutdown cleanup, unfinished-import serve refusal, atomic completion/seed guard and source backup/rollback. Default 1 GiB local cap is configurable (1 byte..5 TiB); no production maximum-size or durability claim.

Body inactivity is suspended during advisory and post-EOF waits, which return 503 backendError after catalog_wait_timeout_ms (default 30000 ms) or the remaining absolute object_request_timeout_ms budget (default 900000 ms). A post-EOF timeout leaves the mutation outcome unknown: the commit may still complete, so re-read state or retry with preconditions. Background filesystem work and shutdown catalog close retain no execution bound; SQLite busy_timeout remains unchanged.
Unreleased schema-v2 catalogs are rejected read-only; automatic migration supports object-free v1 catalogs.

Deferred blob reclamation retries at startup; a repeated failure names the blob ID and blocks readiness until fixed. Ordinary object reclamation retains its startup retry; resumable terminal cleanup additionally has explicit due maintenance and a deadline scheduler.
Lingering close discards at most 256 KiB for 100 ms; early responses are readable on local macOS loopback, without establishing a causal benefit from lingering or every-platform delivery.

SPEC-008: header validation and the known-size check precede immediate upload admission (excess: 503); one advisory bucket 404/condition 412 check precedes streamed-size, body and checksum errors independent of body timing. SPEC-013/SPEC-016: media/multipart upload tokens require ifGenerationMatch with no replay; resumable initiation accepts one nonempty token without it and creates another bounded session; multipart MIME caps/errors, contentType precedence and checksum-container edge rules remain local choices awaiting direct service evidence.

SPEC-RSM-DISCOVERY-PATH/EDGES/AUTH-CONDITIONS: JSON resumable has explicit local edge/error/terminal-retention and permission-recheck choices. All eleven cases pass, including native process kills before offset commit, after acknowledgment, after final checkpoint, after rename and after Object/COMPLETE commit; 20 repeated five-test crash runs pass. Finalization hashes the full object under the request deadline, so latency grows with object size; prepublication error-resolution SQL uses that remaining budget rather than the catalog-wait timeout. These measured/inspected limits and test timing caveats are retained in the evidence; complete provider timeout/error parity is not claimed. Contract: docs/en/slices/resumable-upload.md; evidence: docs/en/evidence/resumable-upload.md. SPEC-RSM-EDGES/AUTH-CONDITIONS retain provider edge and permission-timing questions; no full-provider durability or wire-parity claim.

acceptance_cases.description: Require Content-Length including zero or chunked transfer; missing both returns 411 MissingContentLength; stream exact multiple-buffer bytes through existing bounded storage.
Accept a single valid Content-Type, preserve it through JSON/XML reads and restart, default to application/octet-stream and reject malformed/duplicate values before reading bodies.

Decode Content-MD5 directly as exactly one canonical base64 MD5; reject embedded hash lists, algorithm prefixes, noncanonical padding and conflicting declarations with 400 InvalidDigest; duplicate fields return 400 ExcessHeaderValues and mismatched bytes 400 BadDigest without publication.

Validate x-goog-hash MD5 and big-endian CRC32C separately, comma-combined or in repeated fields; reject duplicate algorithms, malformed values and mismatches under the explicit local checksum-error mapping; unknown algorithms return 501.
Persist Cache-Control and return it through XML GET and JSON metadata GET; reject duplicate fields and reset omitted metadata on overwrite.
Persist a representable Content-Disposition through XML/JSON metadata and restart; reset omitted fields on replacement.
Persist Content-Encoding as metadata for unchanged stored bytes; XML GET with accepted gzip and JSON metadata agree; stored-content-encoding is gzip or identity after replacement.
Persist representable Content-Language through XML/JSON reads and restart; reset it when omitted on replacement.

Normalize custom HTTP metadata keys to lowercase, preserve empty/ASCII values, enforce the 8192-byte stored suffix/value limit and reject empty names, repeated case-folded keys and non-ASCII values under the local representability rule.
Enforce decimal signed-64-bit generation match including zero create-if-absent before body reads and atomically at publication; malformed/duplicate conditions fail without mutation.
Accept one positive decimal metageneration condition alone or paired with generation match, reject malformed/duplicate values and preserve state for stale conditions.
Hyper sends 100-continue only after the adapter accepts headers, authorization, conditions and admission; unsupported/auth/size rejections send final XML errors without reading an advertised body.
Return empty 200, quoted lowercase hexadecimal MD5 ETag, generation, metageneration, whole-object hashes and stored length/encoding, consistent with subsequent XML GET.

Before body reads, explicitly reject ACL/predefined ACL, CSEK/CMEK, class overrides, requester billing, retention/hold, resumable, copy, signing/payload, custom time, unknown query/x-goog and x-amz extensions, ranges, HTTP validators and announced trailers with 501 XML NotImplemented.

Strict local tokens require create and delete for live overwrite through project-plus-bucket grants; allUsers anonymous and allAuthenticatedUsers registered-only writes are distinct; invalid/unsupported credentials never fall back. Permissive writes retain storage semantics.

Use XML errors with local 400 InvalidAuthentication/InvalidDigest/BadDigest/EntityTooLarge, 401 AuthenticationRequired, 403 AccessDenied, authorized 404 NoSuchBucket, 411 MissingContentLength, 412 PreconditionFailed, 501 NotImplemented and 503 ServiceUnavailable.

Rejected headers, permissions, conditions, checksum failures and size excess preserve previous live bytes, metadata, object/history count and generation counter; abandoned blobs/staging are reclaimed.
Configured max bytes succeeds for Content-Length and multi-chunk bodies, while max+1 fails before reading a known-size body or during streaming without replacing prior state.
Two uploads admitted before EOF with the same generation match have exactly one winner, including create-if-absent; failed publication consumes no generation and never overwrites the winner.

Incomplete disconnect, graceful shutdown, process termination, trailers, body inactivity and overall request deadline before EOF cannot publish; recovery preserves prior state and removes abandoned files.
Versioning-enabled overwrite retains historical generations consistently with JSON uploads, including selected old bytes after restart.
The bucket's current default event hold applies at publication, blocks subsequent overwrite without mutation and survives restart.

Reuse bucket-configured XML PUT preflight and actual-response rules on success and errors; denied origin/header rules emit no allow grant and successful preflight confers no write permission. JSON CORS remains unchanged.
Committed XML uploads retain bytes, every supported metadata field, checksums, generation/history and hold state across restart using the existing commit/recovery protocol.
Reuse the two-slot 64 KiB chunk bridge and HTTP max_connections limit; additional incomplete uploads are admitted and aborted requests release capacity without publishing.

features.title: Explicit permissive authentication profile
features.notes: auth_mode=permissive is the default and is selected explicitly by CLI --auth-mode, GCS_MIMIC_AUTH_MODE or JSON auth_mode with the existing precedence. It ignores every Authorization header and credential query parameter and performs no permission checks; the ready event reports auth_mode. Permissive results are never counted as strict coverage. Contract: docs/en/slices/strict-auth.md; evidence: docs/en/evidence/strict-auth.md.

acceptance_cases.description: Without auth settings the ready event reports auth_mode permissive without an identity count; anonymous, unknown bearer, Basic, GOOG4 and duplicate Authorization headers all create, read and upload successfully, and credential query parameters are ignored.

auth_mode follows CLI > environment > JSON file > default precedence; unknown or miscased modes, an empty identity_file, strict without identity_file and identity_file with permissive fail before readiness, catalog creation or listener binding.

features.title: Explicit strict authentication profile
features.notes: Strict local bearer identities enforce additive project/bucket predefined roles on JSON routes and path-style XML reads, including allUsers and registered-only allAuthenticatedUsers. Invalid/unsupported credentials never become anonymous; JSON uses 401 authError and XML uses 400 InvalidAuthentication. Local identities simulate Google identity. Object IAM, ACLs, conditions, custom/basic roles, full UBLA/PAP, remaining signing formats and advanced XML operations, HMAC and gRPC remain unimplemented. Contracts: docs/en/slices/strict-auth.md and docs/en/slices/public-object-reads.md; current evidence: docs/en/evidence/public-object-reads.md. SPEC-017 remains open. Bucket PATCH subset passes Rust/SDK/reference verification: docs/en/evidence/bucket-metadata-patch.md. Keep PARTIAL: the existing pending cases and deviations remain unresolved by PATCH. Bucket PUT replacement cases and local-default limits: docs/en/evidence/bucket-metadata-put.md; scoped final verification passes, and the API client update to v0.308.0 passes the full SDK suite with all dependency inputs CURRENT. V4 RSA signed path-style GET/HEAD is now verified with registered public keys, final Host/port, injected-clock expiry and project/bucket signer permissions; malformed/tampered signatures never become anonymous. Permissive mode explicitly ignores credentials. Contract: docs/en/slices/signed-download.md; evidence: docs/en/evidence/signed-download.md. SPEC-SIGNING-EDGES and SPEC-GO-SIGNER-PORT retain their limits. Any partial V4 field set fails strict authentication, including Date/Expires/SignedHeaders alone. Integrated contract: docs/en/slices/signed-upload.md; final evidence: docs/en/evidence/signed-urls.md.

acceptance_cases.description: On JSON routes, unknown, empty, malformed, duplicate and non-UTF-8 bearer values, Basic/GOOG4/AWS4/bare-token schemes and access_token, oauth_token, X-Goog-Signature, X-Goog-Credential, X-Goog-Algorithm, Signature and GoogleAccessId query parameters (including percent-encoded keys) return 401 authError before body reads or catalog access.

Each supported bucket/object route requires its iam-json permission on the bucket's owning project; viewer, creator, editor, cross-project and role-less callers receive 403 forbidden while permitted calls succeed and rejected mutations leave state unchanged.

objects.insert replacing a live object needs storage.objects.delete: the advisory check rejects it with 403 before the body is read or staged, the publication transaction rechecks it so concurrent creates have one winner, and failing preconditions return 412 first.
Pinned Go SDK clients with static local bearer tokens: object viewer reads/lists but cannot upload, update, delete or get bucket metadata; object creator creates but cannot overwrite or read.

Every strict bucket/object catalog operation (advisory upload checks, publication, media opens, metadata/list/delete) rechecks the authorized bucket project inside its own transaction: a bucket deleted and recreated in another project between authorization and the operation returns 403 without mutation or staging residue; a bucket still missing returns 404 for a caller holding the permission somewhere; a bucket that appears later is re-authorized against its actual project and overwrites still need storage.objects.delete there.

Implement object IAM policies/conditions, ACLs/default ACLs, full UBLA/PAP, V2/HMAC and remaining V4 formats/transports, Google IAM signing, custom/basic roles and gRPC/broader XML enforcement; obtain real-service SPEC-017 wire evidence. Scoped unconditional bucket/public grants and XML reads are verified.
Require storage.buckets.update, enforce project and bucket grants before body and in the transaction; revoked/recreated ownership and policy state stay protected.
Require storage.buckets.update, check project/bucket grants before parsing and transactionally; revoke/recreate races preserve IAM and metadata.

Private V4 RSA GET/HEAD/range, project/bucket signer grants, revocation, startup public-key validation and fail-closed tamper errors; HEAD remains bodyless. Pinned SDK succeeds unmodified at default-port authorities and independently cross-checks explicit ports over HTTP/HTTPS. Any partial V4 field set fails strict authentication, including Date/Expires/SignedHeaders alone.
V4 RSA signed PUT uses local signer create/delete grants, shared atomic conditions and pre-body failure handling.

sdk_evidence.transport: HTTP JSON; explicit endpoint with oauth2.StaticTokenSource local bearer tokens; viewer and creator project-role restrictions
HTTP and trusted HTTPS XML; default-port unmodified SDK signing; independent non-default-port correction (SPEC-GO-SIGNER-PORT)

known_deviations: Scoped local project/bucket predefined roles and public principal sets are enforced. Object IAM, IAM conditions, custom/basic roles, ACLs, full UBLA/PAP, remaining signature formats, HMAC, Google IAM signing and broader transport enforcement remain unimplemented.
Local bearer tokens stand in for Google identity; real OAuth tokens are not verified and are rejected unless registered. Tokens are compared by hash-map lookup, not in constant time.

SPEC-017: authError message/location, the short 403 Forbidden message, the absent WWW-Authenticate header, the missing-bucket 404/403 rule, no extra permission for projection=full and evaluating overwrite preconditions (412) before the overwrite permission (403) are local choices pending real-service evidence.

features.title: Local principal and test-token registry
features.notes: Strict mode loads a bounded (64 KiB) JSON identity registry once at startup: 1..=256 identities with a unique visible-ASCII id, 1..=16 registry-unique bearer tokens and optional project_roles (0..=64 validated project IDs, 1..=32 snapshot roles each). Unknown keys, unknown/basic roles and invalid limits fail startup without a partial load and without echoing tokens. The JSON format replaces the TOML proposal (gaps.json resolved item).
